title: Correctness sweep: watchdog, report open, vendor wait heartbeat, note retry, dash answers
lead: Five small correctness fixes, each found by a review and each reproduced against the code at HEAD: a role that finished cleanly is no longer recorded as hung, a swapped-in FIFO can no longer block a report or render read, a run that waits for a vendor slot keeps its ledger run fresh, `item.note` no longer reports failure after slicer wrote the note, and an owner answer that starts with a dash reaches slicer intact. Every fix starts with a failing test.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
This slice takes the correctness items out of five later-notes rows (owner, 2026-10-31: later-notes rows are folded into sweep slices and the folded rows are retired after this slice is filed). Folded here: S194 item 3 (and item 2 as a question, see below), S195 item 1, S196 item 1, S197 item 1, S203 item 1. The polish items of S194, S195, S196 and S197 go to v1.2 (owner, 2026-10-31); S203 items 2-5 are not in this slice (the orchestrator decides where they go).

1. Clean exit recorded as hung (S194 item 3). `internal/engine/round.go:348` treats `hung()` as final: once the watchdog fired, the round is recorded `hung` and the run pauses as lost, whatever the runner returned. Both vendor adapters return an error only when the cancel killed the process (`internal/agent/claude/run.go:94-96`, `internal/agent/codex/codex.go:262-263`: "a cancel that lands after the process exited does not undo it"). So a role that exits with a good result in the same tick as the watchdog (`internal/engine/watchdog.go:91-98`) comes back with `Exit` ok and a nil error, and is still thrown away as hung. A hung role is the case where the runner returns an error.
2. FIFO or link swapped in (S195 item 1). `readRender` (`internal/engine/approval.go:313-339`) opens with `os.Open` first and checks `ent.Info()` and `f.Stat()` after, so a regular file swapped for a FIFO between the listing and the open blocks the daemon handler in `open(2)` until a writer appears. `readReport` (`internal/engine/report.go:47-77`) checks the listed entry first, but the same swap in the gap between that check and `os.Open` blocks the same way. The role writes both directories, so the file is not ork's. This is reachable only through a swap in that gap, so the severity is low, but the fix is cheap: open with `O_NONBLOCK|O_NOFOLLOW` and keep the existing identity checks. (Verified by reading; the tests below reach the gap with a stale listing entry, as `TestReadRenderRefusesAFileSwappedForALink` does for links.)
3. Wait for a vendor slot goes stale (S196 item 1). The wait for a slot (`internal/engine/round.go:196-216`, `Vendors.AcquireWait`) comes before the ledger step and the heartbeat (`round.go:301`, `heartbeat` at `:634`). While a round waits, the run has no running step and nothing refreshes its `updated_at`. Slicer marks a run with no event for 30 minutes stale (`../slicer/src/slicer/relayrun.py:70,798-805`; a run is exempt only when a step is in phase `wait`, which means waiting on the owner or an approval). `docs/design.md:857-861` says "a ledger heartbeat during the wait is a later slice". This is that slice. The orchestrator step is the one to refresh: it is the run's own step (`internal/engine/states.go:35-42`, `OrchestratorStep`).
4. `item.note` writes twice on retry (S197 item 1). `itemNote` (`internal/daemon/items.go:34-49`) runs `slicer note`, then `d.cache.Refresh`, and returns Refresh's error. `Refresh` returns an error only when the cache is closed or the context ends (`internal/cache/cache.go:393-417`). In both cases slicer already wrote the note, the caller sees a failure and retries, and slicer appends the note again. The note is the write; the refresh is only freshness.
5. Dash-leading answers rejected (S203 item 1). `RelayAnswer` (`internal/slicercli/write.go:354-367`) passes `--option VALUE`, `--text VALUE` and `--by VALUE` as two arguments. Slicer's parser is argparse. A value that starts with `-` and has no space ("-fast", "-x") is read as a flag, and the command fails with "expected one argument". Checked on 2026-10-31 against the installed slicer: `relay-run answer` shows `--option LABEL`, `--text TEXT`, `--by NAME` in its usage, and in a scratch project `slicer relay-roles set r1 --model -x` was refused while `--model=-x` was accepted. `adj` takes the same values without trouble (`adj decide 999999 --text -x --why -y --by -z` reaches "record not found": adjudicate parses flags with Go's `flag`, `../adjudicate/internal/cli/cli.go:230`), so `internal/adjcli/adjcli.go` stays as it is.

Not in this slice:
- S194 item 2 (do real Claude and Codex send events during a long silent tool call, so the 30 minutes cannot kill a healthy role). It is a measurement, not a code defect, and it needs billed vendor calls. See the manifest question; if the owner approves the probe, the orchestrator adds it as a step.
- The other `os.ReadFile` reads of role-written report paths (`internal/engine/round.go:578`, `internal/engine/speccheck.go:328`, `internal/agent/claude/report.go:17`, `internal/agent/codex/codex.go:280`) have the same shape. They run in the engine's own goroutines, not in a daemon handler; not changed here.
- The same refresh-after-write pattern in `internal/daemon/adjwrite.go:30,52` and `internal/daemon/relayanswer.go:115`; not changed here.
- Dash-leading values for `slicer note --text` and the other write verbs.
- All polish items of S194 (1, 4, 5), S195 (2-6), S196 (2-10), S197 (2-8), S203 (2-5).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Engine, `internal/engine/watchdog_test.go`:
- `TestRoleThatFinishesAsTheWatchdogFiresIsNotRecordedHung`: a role (limit 50ms, real clock, as `hungHarness` sets up) waits for its context to end and then returns `defaultResult(req), nil`, as an adapter does when the process exited before the cancel landed. Expect the run to reach `StateAwaitingApproval`, `Roles[0].Exit == "ok"`, no `PendingLost`, and no step ended `fail`. Fails first: `hung()` is true, so the run pauses lost with exit `hung`.
- The existing `TestSilentRoleIsKilledAfterTheLimitAndTheRunPausesAsLost`, `TestHungRoleDoesNotFallBackOrMarkAVendorOut` and `TestTwoHungSiblingRoundsPauseOnce` must keep passing (their fake runner returns `ctx.Err()`).

Engine, `internal/engine/fifo_unix_test.go`:
- `TestReadRenderDoesNotBlockOnAFileSwappedForAFIFO`: list a directory with one regular `a-80x24.txt`, keep the `os.ReadDir` entry, replace the file with a FIFO (`syscall.Mkfifo`), call `readRender(dir, entry)` in a goroutine, and require it to return within 2 seconds with `errNotThatFile`. Fails first: `os.Open` blocks (the test then opens the FIFO `O_RDWR` to release the goroutine and fails).
- `TestReadReportDoesNotBlockOnAFileSwappedForAFIFO`: the same for `readReport(dir, entry)` with the `listedReportEntry` helper from `readreport_test.go` (it returns the identity captured at listing time); expect `ok == false` within 2 seconds. Fails first: blocks.
- `TestReadRenderAndReadReportRefuseASymlinkAtOpen`: with the same stale-entry technique and a symlink in place, both return the refusal (this passes today through the identity check; it pins that `O_NOFOLLOW` did not loosen it). The existing `TestReadRenderRefusesAFileSwappedForALink` and `TestReadReportRefusesLinksPathsAndOtherFiles` keep passing.
- `TestOpenNoBlockReadsARegularFile`: a regular file opens and reads in full through `openNoBlock`.

Engine, `internal/engine/heartbeat_test.go`:
- `TestVendorSlotWaitSendsHeartbeatsOnTheOrchestratorStep`: `heartbeatEngine(t)`; set `OrchestratorStep` to `orch-1` with `e.run.Update`; give the engine `e.d.Vendors = NewVendors(map[string]int{"claude": 1})` and take the only slot in the test; run `runRound` in a goroutine (the harness implementer row is vendor `claude`); require a `relay-run step --step orch-1 --phase start` call with no `--task` within 2 seconds while the slot is held, and no role step started yet. Release the slot, let the round finish, then require that the heartbeat stopped (no `orch-1` call after the round returned). Fails first: no call is made during the wait.
- `TestVendorSlotWaitWithoutAnOrchestratorStepSendsNoHeartbeat`: the same wait with `OrchestratorStep` empty makes no `relay-run step` call before the slot is released.
- `TestImmediateVendorSlotSendsNoOrchestratorHeartbeat`: a free slot makes no `orch-1` call (the heartbeat interval is `time.Hour`, as `TestShortRoundSendsNoHeartbeat` sets it).

Daemon, `internal/daemon/items_test.go`:
- `TestItemNoteSucceedsWhenTheItemsRefreshFails`: with the same fake slicer route as `TestItemNoteWritesTheNoteAndReadsItemsAgain`, close the cache (`d.cache.Close()`) before the call so `Refresh` returns `cache.ErrClosed`. Expect `item.note` to return `{"item":"S12"}` and no error, with exactly one `slicer note` call. Fails first: the handler returns the cache error. (If closing the cache does not produce the error in the harness, cancel the request context between the write and the refresh instead; the assertion is the same.)
- The existing `TestItemNoteKeepsTheSlicerErrorCode` and `TestItemNoteRefusals` keep passing: a failed `slicer note` is still an error.

Slicer client, `internal/slicercli/write_test.go`:
- `TestRelayAnswerKeepsADashLeadingValueAttached`: for `{Option: "-fast"}`, `{Text: "-x"}` and `{Text: "ok", By: "-bob"}` the argv is `relay-run answer RUN Q --option=-fast`, `--text=-x`, `--text=ok --by=-bob`, each followed by `--json --root ROOT`. Fails first: the values are separate arguments.
- Update `TestRelayAnswerPassesOptionOrTextAndBy` to the attached form (`--option=Database`, `--text=keep files`, `--by=Jon R`); it fails first for the same reason and then pins the new argv.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Tests first, in the order above; run each new test and see it fail for the stated reason before the fix.

1. Watchdog (`internal/engine/round.go:348`). Change the check to `if hung() && runErr != nil`. Update the comment above it: a runner that returns without an error finished by itself, so a result that came back in the tick the watchdog fired is the role's real result. Do not change `watchdog.go`. Leave `stopWatch`, `release` and the `ctx.Err()` branch above it as they are.
2. Report and render open. Add `openNoBlock(path)` in `openfile_unix.go`: `os.OpenFile(path, os.O_RDONLY|syscall.O_NONBLOCK|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW, 0)`. In `openfile_other.go` it is `os.Open`. Use it in `readReport` and `readRender` in place of `os.Open`, and keep the `Stat`, `Lstat` and `SameFile` checks after the open exactly as they are (they are what refuse a FIFO that opened without blocking). Check that a regular file still reads in full with `O_NONBLOCK` set (`TestOpenNoBlockReadsARegularFile`).
3. Vendor wait heartbeat (`internal/engine/round.go:196-216`). Before the slot loop, start `e.heartbeat(ctx, rec, id)` where `id` is `rec.OrchestratorStep`, or `""` when `rec.RelayRun == ""`, `rec.OrchestratorStep == ""` or `rec.Commit != nil` (the guards `stepStart` and `orchestratorPhase` use). Stop it as soon as the loop has a slot, and on every error return inside the loop. Do not add a new ledger phase: the heartbeat is the same `--phase start` call the role heartbeat sends. Update `docs/design.md:857-861`: the wait keeps the run's ledger run fresh by a heartbeat on the orchestrator step every 10 minutes; the Running row cue is unchanged.
4. Note retry (`internal/daemon/items.go:45`). After a successful `Slicer.Note`, ignore the refresh error: keep the call (the cache then reads fresh items when it can) and return `&ItemNoteResult{Item: p.Item}, nil`. Add a one-line comment that the note is the write and the refresh only freshness. Update the `item.note` row in `docs/design.md:103` to say a failed refresh after the write is not an error. Do not change `itemNew` or the adj and relay answer handlers.
5. Dash-leading answers (`internal/slicercli/write.go:354-367`). Build the three flags as one attached argument each: `"--option=" + spec.Option`, `"--text=" + spec.Text`, `"--by=" + spec.By`. Keep the order, the `--json` tail and the choice between option and text. Do not touch `internal/adjcli`. Do not change `Note`, `Edit` or `RelayAsk`.
6. Docs: `docs/design.md:743-757` gets one sentence: a role that came back with a result and no error in the tick the watchdog fired is recorded as it exited.
7. `CHANGELOG.md`: add one entry under `## Unreleased` last, so that a parallel slice's entry does not conflict. Name the five fixes in one paragraph; mark the vendor wait heartbeat *proposed* (it adds ledger traffic beyond the roadmap).
8. Do not touch: `internal/engine/watchdog.go`, the vendor adapters, `internal/adjcli`, `internal/tui`, and the polish items listed above.
